column1: # scripts/stacks.tsv: one row per stack. Read through scripts/stacks.js, its one reader, by scripts/on-manifest-change.js (restore after a merge), scripts/format-changed.js (pre-push format check) and the project-init skill (scaffold). Commands run through the OS shell.

# Columns, tab-separated: stack | triggers: file patterns, space-separated, matched by path or basename | needs: a file that must exist at the root for the row to fire, or - | restore: command run from the repo root, or - | scaffold: commands joined by " && " with {Name} PascalCase, {name} kebab-case, {template} chosen by project-init, or - | formats: patterns of the files a push publishes that this row formats, or - | format: check-only command, {files} replaced by those paths, or - to skip. Fallbacks separated by " ?? " are tried in order until one tool is installed (the dotnet row prefers a project Husky.NET task runner, then dotnet format). It must not rewrite files; the hook reports and blocks, and git push --no-verify skips it. The formats cell is the contract and the format command trusts it, so the prettier rows pass no --ignore-unknown and an extension prettier cannot parse fails loudly; ADR-0003 is why, and which extensions that admits. The dotnet row loads the project first, so it costs 5-15s on a push touching C#: blank the cell to opt out. A row whose triggers are - only scaffolds: dotnet-aspire is the .NET scaffold for the microservices unit type, and the dotnet row restores and format-checks what it creates.
